Raul (customer): Hey team — hitting a weird failure with the embeddings endpoint. We're sending a batch of 3 texts but getting a 400 and the response says "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024". We're using the `text-embed-001` model. Request payload below:

Raul (customer): ```json
{
  "input": [["first doc"], "second doc", "third doc"],
  "model": "text-embed-001"
}
```

Raul (customer): Also, when we try single-item calls we sometimes get a 200 but the vector length still varies. Any hints? :confused:

Maya (client-dev): @Raul two quick suspects: (1) your `input` shape is inconsistent (notice the nested array for the first doc) and (2) maybe you're accidentally calling a different model variant client-side. Can you paste the exact curl or SDK call? :eyes:

Raul (customer): Here's our python snippet (requests):

Raul (customer): ```python
payload = {
    "input": [["first doc"], "second doc", "third doc"],
    "model": "text-embed-001"
}
resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
```

Alice (support): Thanks — yep that nested list is likely it. The embeddings endpoint expects either a single string or an array of strings at the top level: `input: "a single text"` or `input: ["one","two"]`. When the client sends mixed nesting we sometimes trigger internal batching logic that misroutes to a quantized variant which uses 1024 dims. We should be able to reproduce locally.

Priya (sre): Note: we also had a small routing rollout last night for a lower-dim experimental alias. Unlikely to affect well-formed requests but mixed shapes could hit the alias. I'm checking routing logs for Raul's request id if he can share.

Raul (customer): Request id is `req_0a3f9b`. Also saw `401` once earlier — was that because of expired token? We rotated keys recently.

Alice (support): 401 would be auth — separate. For the dimension issue, quick repro steps: send a single top-level list of strings and confirm dims. For example:

Alice (support): ```bash
curl -X POST $URL -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '\"{\\"input\\": [\\"first doc\\", \\\"second doc\\"], \\\"model\\\": \\\"text-embed-001\\\"}\\\''
```

Alice (support): If that returns 1536 vectors you were hitting the shape problem. If not, paste the raw response.

Maya (client-dev): Also check encoding: if you build payload via `json.dumps` vs manual concatenation, sometimes non-utf8 or stray arrays sneak in. If you're using numpy arrays on the client convert to lists first — numpy serialization can produce nested arrays unexpectedly.

Raul (customer): Quick test: changed to `input: ["first doc","second doc","third doc"]` and now all three returned length 1536. So that fixed it. Thanks! But we still saw intermittent 1024 in our logs last week — could that be the routing rollout you mentioned?

Priya (sre): I've correlated `req_0a3f9b` and a few adjacent reqs to a canary pool that includes an experimental quantized model. The routing decision uses a hash of the request signature which included the serialized payload. Mixed shapes can yield unexpected signatures. We'll mark that as a hazard in the rollout notes.

Raul (customer): Appreciate it. Any recommendations to prevent this on our side?

Alice (support): Best practices: always normalize inputs before call — coerce to top-level list even for single item: `inputs = [x] if isinstance(x, str) else x`. Validate shapes client-side and add a CI test that calls the embeddings endpoint and asserts vector length == expected (1536). Also add a small retry-on-dimension-mismatch that logs the full payload.

Maya (client-dev): Sample JS snippet for safety:```js
function normalizeInput(inp){
  if (typeof inp === 'string') return [inp];
  if (!Array.isArray(inp)) throw new Error('unsupported input');
  // flatten only one level, reject nested arrays
  if (inp.some(i => Array.isArray(i))) throw new Error('nested arrays not allowed');
  return inp;
}
```

Raul (customer): We'll roll that in. One more thing — throughput: when we switched from single calls to batching we saw latency drop but some calls 429'd. Is there a recommended batch size?

Alice (support): For text-embed-001 we recommend batches of up to 64 small texts (~<=256 tokens). If you have mixed long docs, size by token count. Also enable exponential backoff on 429/5xx. Our console has per-route limits that vary by account tier; I can check your quota and open a burst allowance if needed.

Sam (support-mgr): Looping in: @Priya please add an engineering note about the routing sensitivity to serialized payload shapes. @Alice flag this as a docs update — we should call out nested arrays explicitly in the embeddings guide and show common client pitfalls (numpy arrays, single vs list).

Priya (sre): Will do. I'll also add a short-term guard in the canary router to avoid experimental model selection if payload shape isn't canonical.

Raul (customer): thanks all — resolved on our end. Leaving the thread open in case you want extra logs from our SDKs. :+1:

Alice (support): Great, marking as resolved from support side but please ping if you hit the 1024 vector again. We'll follow up when the router guard is deployed.
